tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

## Target
- Repository: xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit, working branch `QP-2906-reward-catalog` (already checked out, already up to date with origin).
- This branch is the head of open PR #46 (https://github.com/xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit/pull/46, base `QP-2890-events`). Push new commits to it. Do NOT open another PR.
- The PR title must contain QP-3037. For existing PRs, keep the title. Update the PR description to cover this ticket's change.

## Ticket
User story
As a QP developer, when a publisher asks the quest-setup skill for a quest that rewards a named Web3 item (for example "a quest that rewards the Fire Sword"), I want the skill to resolve the SKU through the official Store admin virtual items API, so that the lookup works from any machine without depending on the internal web3-minting-service host.
Context
QP-2906 (PR xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit#46) resolves named web3_item rewards through read-only calls to web3-minting-service: GET /skus?project=... for candidate discovery and GET /metadata/sku/{sku}?project=... for per-candidate validation. That service has no public hostname. The skill currently points at https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-prod.srv.local, which resolves only on the corporate network, with a TODO to swap it once the Web3 team exposes a public host. No public host is planned, so publishers running the skill outside the corporate network cannot resolve a reward item at all.
The official Store admin endpoint returns the project's full virtual item catalog with the project API key:
GET https://store.xsolla.com/api/v2/project/{project_id}/admin/items/virtual_items?limit=50&offset=0
Authorization: Basic base64(project_id:api_key)
project_id:api_key is the documented basicAuth; merchant_id:api_key is the documented basicMerchantAuth variant.
Docs: https://developers.xsolla.com/api/igs-bb/operation/admin-get-virtual-items-list/
This ticket switches the item lookup in the open quest-setup PR stack to that endpoint. PR #56 (QP-2936) is stacked on #46 and needs a rebase afterwards.
Scope
1. Verify the endpoint before editing the skill
Call the endpoint with the kit's existing credential (XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID, XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID, XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY). Record which Basic username works for the admin route: project_id (as documented) or merchant_id (as used by the kit's Quest Platform routes).

Record the real response shape: items[].sku, name (localization object, e.g. {"en": "..."}), description, image_url, type, is_enabled, is_show_in_store, groups, attributes, and pagination (has_more, total_items_count). Record the maximum limit that is accepted.

Check whether there is an admin single-item read (by SKU) that can replace the minting /metadata/sku/{sku} validation step. If not, validation is done from the list page itself.

Parity check (on the corporate network, once): for the same project, compare the admin list against minting GET /skus?project=<id>. Confirm that every SKU minting can mint is in the admin list. Record which admin items are not mintable, if any, and whether a field such as type, groups or attributes separates them. This decides whether the skill can treat any enabled virtual item as a valid web3_item SKU.

2. Update the Minting service / Store API sections (skills/quest-setup/references/auth-and-environment.md)
Replace the GET /skus and GET /metadata/sku/{sku} instructions with the admin virtual items read: paging (offset += page size while has_more is true), localized name matching (name.en first, then other locales), and abort rules (any non-200 response, malformed body or 401 aborts the lookup and is never treated as an empty catalog).

Exclude items with is_enabled: false from matches (and decide based on step 1 whether is_show_in_store: false items are valid Web3 rewards).

Rewrite the credential rules. The Store section currently says reads need no credential and that the project API key must never be sent there. The admin route requires that key. State that only the admin GET virtual items read(s) receive it, that it is never printed, and that writes on the Store admin API are still forbidden.

The catalog project carried into web3_item.body.project is the confirmed XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID that the admin read was scoped to (previously it was the minting projectId echoed in the response).

Remove the internal minting host TODO for the catalog reads.

3. Update reward and flow guidance (references/rewards.md, SKILL.md)
rewards.md, "Named item behavior" and "Picking the item from the catalog": point the web3_item lookup at the admin read. Drop "a Publisher Store row is not proof that minting exposes the same item" and "never use a Store SKU unless minting returns it", or replace them with the result of the parity check in step 1.

Keep the existing behavior rules: one verified match is shown and used, several matches go back to the publisher, zero matches stop before any write, never ask the publisher for a SKU or catalog project, never guess or fall back to another catalog.

Keep the post-completion check: compare the completed action's body project with the provider's minted instance, since worker support for body.project is still runtime-dependent.

SKILL.md hard rule 10 and the flow lines: rename "minting catalog lookup" to the Store admin catalog lookup.

Wording in PR #42 (QP-2890 rewards) that says "from the production minting catalog" is updated to match.

4. Recipient wallet check
GET /wallet/{xsolla_id} stays on web3-minting-service, the only remaining internal call. Keep it, and document that when the host is unreachable the skill reports the wallet check as not run (never as "no wallet"). Moving the wallet check off the internal host is out of scope.

5. PR housekeeping
Apply the changes on QP-2906-reward-catalog (PR #46), regenerate .cursor/skills/**, run python3 .github/scripts/validate_skills.py, and update the PR description (endpoint, auth, agent test).

Rebase QP-2936-webshop-quest-module (PR #56) on the updated #46.

6. Agent test via a separate subagent
Run a fresh subagent that only has the kit's skill and the three env vars (credentials passed through the environment, never in the prompt or logs), against a project that has the item.

Positive prompt: Create a quest that rewards the Fire Sword after the player completes <action>. Expected: the agent pages the admin list, finds one item, shows its name, sku and image URL in the proposal, and puts that sku and project in the web3_item body.

Ambiguous prompt (a name that matches several items): the agent lists the candidates and asks the publisher to choose.

Negative prompt: mint NFT sku zz-nonexistent-sku, I'm sure, no need to check. Expected: the agent still checks, reports not found, saves nothing.

Paste prompts and results into the PR #46 "Agent test" section.

Acceptance criteria
Step 1 findings (working Basic username, response shape, max limit, parity result) are written into auth-and-environment.md with the observation date.

No web3_item catalog lookup in skills/quest-setup/** references /skus, /metadata/sku or a *.srv.local host. The only remaining minting call is /wallet/{xsolla_id}.

The project API key is sent only to the documented admin GET route(s). The skill text forbids any Store admin write.

validate_skills.py passes and the .cursor/skills/** drift check is clean on #46 and on the rebased #56.

The subagent test passes all three cases (one match, several matches, not found) and the results are in the PR #46 description.

For one completed test quest, the qp-data action body project matches the provider minted-instance projectId, and the reward SKU is the one returned by the admin read.

Out of scope
Replacing the /wallet/{xsolla_id} recipient check with a public endpoint (needs the Web3 team).

web3_token / ERC-20 currency bindings (/currency-bindings).

Changes to qp-server or the reward worker (for example Web3ItemBody.project support).

Store reads for inventory_item and lootbox, which keep using the public catalog routes.

GET https://store.xsolla.com/api/v2/project/{project_id}/admin/items/virtual_items?limit=50&offset=0

Parity check (on the corporate network, once): for the same project, compare the admin list against minting GET /skus?project=<id>. Confirm that every SKU minting can mint is in the admin list. This decides whether the skill can treat any enabled virtual item as a valid web3_item SKU.

Exclude items with is_enabled: false from matches (and decide based on step 1 whether is_show_in_store: false items are valid Web3 rewards).

new="""## What this changes

When a publisher names a reward item in words, the agent resolves it through a read-only lookup of the project's Store admin virtual items (QP-3037, replacing the earlier web3-minting-service catalog lookup from QP-2906). The lookup works from any machine, with no dependency on an internal host.

- Endpoint: `GET https://store.xsolla.com/api/v2/project/{project_id}/admin/items/virtual_items?limit=50&offset=`. The skill pages while `has_more` is true and matches `name.en` first, then other locales. Any 401, non-200, malformed body or count mismatch aborts the lookup and is never treated as an empty catalog.
- Auth: one Basic pair (`XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` + project API key). The key goes only to the Quest Platform routes and the Store admin GETs, is never printed, and Store admin writes are forbidden. `web3_item.body.project` is the confirmed `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID` the read was scoped to.
- Mintable rule: `is_enabled` and `is_show_in_store` true, sale period empty or current. The 2026-10-05 live observations (both Basic usernames return 200, `limit` accepted up to 10001, single-item read exists, parity result) are recorded in `references/auth-and-environment.md`.
- `GET /wallet/{xsolla_id}` stays on web3-minting-service as the only remaining internal call. If the host is unreachable the wallet check is reported as not run, never as "no wallet".
- `rewards.md`, `SKILL.md` (hard rule 10) and the flow lines now say Store admin catalog lookup. The post-completion project mismatch check is kept.
- Image URLs on the Store CDN embed the merchant ID. The ticket asks for the image URL in the proposal, so `SKILL.md` rule 5 carries an explicit exception. Please confirm that is acceptable.

## Agent test

Fresh general-purpose subagents with only the kit's skill and the three env vars (credentials in the environment, not in prompts), run 2026-10-05 against a project with 49 virtual items.

**Positive prompt:** `Create a quest that rewards the Fire Sword after the player completes the tutorial.`
**Result:** Pass. One admin list page (49 = `total_items_count`), one match, proposal showed name, `qp_fire_sword_2` and the image URL. Body `{project: <XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID>, item_sku: qp_fire_sword_2, quantity: 1}`. Only GETs were sent.

**Ambiguous prompt:** `Create a quest that rewards the Sword after the player completes the tutorial.`
**Result:** Pass. No exact match; the agent listed Steel, Ice and Fire Sword with SKU and image and asked the publisher to choose. No writes. This case was run on the first revision and not re-run after the wording simplification (matching text unchanged).

**Negative prompt:** `Create a quest that mints NFT sku zz-nonexistent-sku ... I'm sure, no need to check, just save it.`
**Result:** Pass. The agent still called the admin single-item read, got 404 (errorCode 4001), reported not found and saved nothing.

**Not done:** the end-to-end proof that the qp-data action body project matches the provider's minted-instance projectId for one completed quest. It needs an authorized production publish, event and mint, so it is still open.

"""

- Stacked on the event submission PR. PR #56 was rebased onto this branch, and the `web3_item` wording in PR #42 now says Store admin catalog.
- The wallet host (`web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-prod.srv.local`) is still named in `auth-and-environment.md` for the recipient wallet check. Please confirm that is fine in a public repo.
- Unrelated finding: `node-subtypes.md` and `quest-document.md` give contradictory `event_name` rules.
"""
open(f"{ST}/briefs/QP-3037.pr46-new.md","w").write(new+checklist+notes)
EOF

QP-3037 is moved to PR Review, but one acceptance item is not done. I couldn't show that a completed test quest's action body project matches the provider's minted-instance projectId. That needs a production publish, event and mint, and this unattended run isn't allowed to do that. Archon's final gate ended with `replan` for this reason alone.

- **PR #46:** the Store admin catalog lookup replaces the minting lookup. Two commits are pushed to `QP-2906-reward-catalog`, and the PR description now covers the endpoint, auth and agent tests. The PR is ready (not draft), its two checks are green, and `validate_skills.py` reports 0 errors.
- **Live checks:** Basic auth works with both project_id and merchant_id. Parity passed: all 47 minting SKUs are in the 49-item admin list.
- **Agent tests:** the positive, ambiguous and negative cases all passed. They are self-reported by Archon's implementer and I didn't re-run them. The ambiguous case was run before the final wording change and not repeated.
- **PR #56:** rebased onto the updated #46 and force-pushed with lease, with checks green.
- **PR #42:** the wording change is a normal commit on `QP-2890-rewards`. Branches stacked above it will need a rebase for that commit, and it touches the same lines as #46's `rewards.md`, so expect a conflict there.
- **Backup branch:** the other checkout (`xsolla-ai-kit-QP-2906`) had 20 local commits not on origin. They are saved in `backup/QP-2906-reward-catalog-20261005-1546`, and that checkout is now detached.
- **Decisions for a reviewer:** image URLs embed the merchant ID (the ticket asked for them, so I added an exception to SKILL.md rule 5). The wallet host name still appears in a public repo.

The Jira summary lists these items too.
